ble_soc.airtag_part: Nordic nRF52832-CIAA (WLCSP) — part marking read by lane A off full-resolution board photos; corroborated by iFixit / TechInsights / Catley
ble_soc.parity_target: nRF54L10 per DECISIONS.md D12; nRF54L05 fallback, nRF54L15 step-up. Supersedes D10's nRF52840-class target.
ble_soc.why_v1: nRF54L10 carries Bluetooth Channel Sounding (lane H measured 6-10 cm mean error on coin-cell nRF54L15 hardware), keeps NFC-A so there is still no NFC BOM line, is $1.74/unit cheaper than nRF52840 at 1k, and is the only nRF54L variant with both stock (669 LCSC / 1003 JLCPCB) and enough memory. Cost of the move is a firmware port: every existing Find My implementation targets nRF52 silicon.
ble_soc.why_d10_pick_was: nRF52840 meets the D10 parity target, keeps the NFC-A peripheral that lets the tap-to-see-owner flow work with no NFC chip at all, has 1 MB flash so the external NOR can be deleted, and is in 51k LCSC stock. nRF52832 (C77540) remains the gen-1 exact die and the cheaper option at $2.6440/1k.

options.note: Only the R7 reel is in stock. LCSC stock 669, JLCPCB 1003 at pull; minimum packet 1000.
Deepest stock of the three (1775) and cheapest. Whether firmware fits 0.5 MB / 96 kB decides $0.39/unit.
The part lane H measured Channel Sounding on - but ZERO stock at LCSC and JLCPCB at pull. A paper option today.

ble_module_nrf54l.question: lane I asked: does any pre-certified castellated module built on an nRF54L part exist today, and does it expose the NFC antenna pins?
ble_module_nrf54l.answer: YES for Raytac. The AN54LQ family covers nRF54L05/L10/L15, is certified in nine regimes including Japanese Telec/Giteki, and its pin table documents NFC1 on pad 15 and NFC2 on pad 16. Pad STYLE (castellated vs LGA) could not be confirmed from the spec PDF text - the drawing is an image. Nothing is in stock anywhere.
ble_module_nrf54l.recommended: Raytac AN54LQ-P10 (nRF54L10, PCB antenna) once Raytac confirms stock, MOQ, lead time and pad style

options.pad_style: UNCONFIRMED - 42 pads with a documented land pattern; castellation likely (Raytac MDBT42Q precedent) but not proven from the spec text
options.bt_qualification: BT6 certified; 'a recommended 3rd-party module by Nordic Semiconductor'
options.note: NO PRICE FETCHED for the -10. Not listed at LCSC, JLCPCB or in the Digi-Key module filter; Mouser timed out.
Larger-memory sibling, so this is an UPPER BOUND on the AN54LQ-10 price. Zero stock.
Smallest nRF54L module found. LGA 0.65 mm pitch, so not hand-solderable and not castellated. Certifications stated only generically ('FCC, CE, Telec, etc.') on the overview page.
Listed in the JLCPCB catalogue with PLACEHOLDER prices on zero stock. Vendor page fetch failed (socket closed) - specs, NFC pin exposure and certifications NOT VERIFIED.

ble_module_precertified.airtag_part: none — Apple certified the whole product, not a module
ble_module_precertified.why: Carries an nRF52840 (verified from the part page HTML), so it meets D10 parity, and it is the only Nordic module in real JLCPCB stock at pull; moves intentional-radiator testing to the vendor under 47 CFR 15.212. Its certification list did NOT render on Ebyte's page — treat FCC/CE/Giteki as unverified until the vendor's cert PDFs are in hand.

uwb_transceiver.airtag_part: Apple U1 SiP (AirTag 2: Apple U2) — not purchasable, no substitute is pin- or protocol-compatible with Apple Precision Finding without MFi
uwb_transceiver.why: The only UWB part with a public MFi Apple-U1-interoperability certification, and the same DW3000 core inside Qorvo's own DWM3001C. For haytag-uwb it is used tag-to-tag, so no Apple handshake is involved.

options.note: Two RX ports — the part to pick if the fleet needs angle of arrival, not just range.
Cheapest at LCSC and in real stock there, QFN not WLCSP so far easier to hand-place, but 3.5-6.5 GHz only, no 802.15.4z, no Apple interop, and much worse sleep than DW3000.
DW3110 + nRF52833 + planar UWB antenna + accelerometer in one pre-certified module. Too big for a 30 mm puck and ~7x the silicon cost, but it is the zero-RF-layout route for an embedded host board.

nfc.airtag_part: NO NFC IC EXISTS ON THE BOARD. Lane A: the Nordic SoC's own NFC-A peripheral drives the coil directly from pins P0.09 and P0.10. Catley independently identifies the tag as a read-only MIFARE Plus (Type 4) implemented in the SoC.
nfc.bom_line: deleted - cost is one PCB coil (copper, $0) plus two tuning capacitors
nfc.recommended: on-chip NFC-A of the nRF52840/nRF52832 (cost $0), with NT3H2111W0FHKH as the fallback ONLY if a non-NFC SoC is chosen
nfc.why: DULT serial lookup and Apple's tap-to-see-owner flow both need only a readable NDEF URL; the SoC already has the radio and the antenna is PCB copper.

options.note: Needs two NFC pins, a PCB coil and 2 tuning caps. Cost is the coil area, not a part.
NXP NT3H2111 NTAG I2C plus, XQFN-8 1.6x1.6 mm, 53k in stock — best discrete NFC option.
Same die, SO-8. Nearly 4x the price of the XQFN and 17 in stock.
NTAG213 (NT2H1311) HXSON-4 — read-only NDEF, no I2C side, cheapest true NTAG in stock.
ST ST25DV04K UDFN-12 — ISO 15693 + NFC, energy harvesting output.

accelerometer.why: BMA280 is effectively unsourceable (LCSC stock 29, MOQ 10 000). LIS2DW12 is the closest always-on low-power 3-axis part with real stock, sub-1 uA low-power mode and the same wake/motion interrupt engine the AirTag's 10 s / 0.5 s sampling scheme needs.

options.note: THE Apple part. LCSC stock 29, minimum packet 10 000 — cannot be bought in prototype quantity.

options.lp_current: <1 uA in low-power mode, 90 uA high-resolution

options.note: LIS2DH12: cheaper still, older, coarser.

BMA456: in stock (2839) but 4x the LIS2DW12 price.
Famous for ~0.5 uA sniff mode but zero stock and no volume break published.

sounder_transducer.settled_by: lane G: a bare Murata 7BB-20-3 piezo bender bonded to the shell, not a housed buzzer and not a micro-speaker
sounder_transducer.airtag_part: custom voice coil glued to the plastic shell, driven against a fixed magnet in the middle of the donut PCB — the shell is the diaphragm (Catley/iFixit). No purchasable equivalent.
sounder_transducer.recommended: Murata 7BB-20-3 (bare piezo bender, lane G) - NOT in the LCSC/JLCPCB catalogue; priced from sibling 7BB-20-6C
sounder_transducer.why_housed_was_picked: A magnetic (not piezo) transducer keeps the AirTag's tonal character and is the loudest thing that fits an 8 mm puck off the shelf. iFixit notes the piezo tags (Tile, SmartTag) were as loud or louder, so nothing acoustic is lost by not copying the voice coil; what is lost is the AirTag's timbre.

flash.airtag_part: GigaDevice GD25LE32 or GD25LQ32, 32 Mbit SPI NOR (lane A read the marking; iFixit says GD25LE32D)
flash.why: Apple needed 32 Mbit for U1 firmware, audio assets and logs. A haytag whose firmware lives in the nRF52840's own 1 MB does not need an external flash at all; dropping it removes $0.41-1.45 and 8 joints.

options.note: Cheapest at 1k and same family as Apple's part - the pick if flash comes back.
GD25LE32E, the LE half of lane A's reading. LCSC stock 37.
Winbond W25Q32JW, 1.8 V, 11 903 in stock.

bulk_capacitance.airtag_part: five 100 uF capacitors (lane A counted them off the board)
bulk_capacitance.why: A CR2032 has 10-15 ohm internal resistance fresh and much more when aged; ~500 uF of bulk is what lets a coin cell drive a voice coil or a UWB burst without browning out the SoC. Qorvo's own DW3000 DC table qualifies single-frame TX/RX 'with 47uF capacitor'. This is the second-largest line in the haytag BOM after the SoC.

options.note: CCTC 0805 100 uF 6.3 V, 11 262 in stock. 5x = $1.54 at 1k.
Cheapest ceramic: 5x = $1.04 at 1k, saving $0.50/unit. Only 2 057 in stock.
Samsung CL21A107MQYNNWE, the name-brand option, 11 620 in stock, 5x = $1.90 at 1k.
Tantalum: cheapest of all (5x = $0.67 at 500) and no DC-bias derating, but taller and with a failure mode you may not want next to a coin cell.

power.airtag_part: TI TPS62746 300 mA buck + ON Semi FPF2487 OVP load switch (iFixit)
power.recommended: direct-from-cell for haytag-core; TPS7A0233 LDO only for the UWB rail in haytag-uwb
power.why: nRF52832 runs 1.7-3.6 V so a CR2032 feeds it directly with no regulator; Apple needed the buck because the U1 and the 1.8 V flash needed a rail the cell cannot hold under pulse load. DW3110 is 1.5-3.6 V but its 14-23 mA bursts need a bulk cap; the DW3000 datasheet itself specifies single-frame TX/RX 'with 47uF capacitor'.

options.note: The Apple part (TPS62746, DSBGA-8). LCSC stock 0 at pull.
NO PRICE - keyword search of the JLCPCB parts catalogue on 2026-09-03 returned zero hits. Not needed: its job was protecting the U1 rail.
TPS7A0233 3.3 V nano-quiescent LDO, SOT-23-5, 5 649 in stock.
XC6206P332MR-G — a JLCPCB Basic part, so no feeder fee. 3 uA quiescent is poor for a coin cell; use only where the rail is switched.
nRF52832 supply range 1.7-3.6 V covers a CR2032 from fresh to end of life; the AirTag itself powers up from 2 V (Catley).

battery_and_contacts.why: SMD holder, 10 300 in stock, and it survives reflow; the bent contacts are cheaper but need a mechanical retainer in the shell.

options.note: ONLY the qty-1 price was fetched; volume breaks were not. Used as an upper bound at every quantity in the roll-up.
Cheapest route ($0.024 at 10k) and the closest to what Apple does — a stamped spring against a shell-retained cell.
Through-hole holder, $0.064 at 5k.
